1: Paul thanks God for the Colossians' faith. Then he praises Christ: the image of the invisible God, through whom and for whom all things were made, head of the Church, the firstborn from the dead, who made peace by the blood of his cross.
Jesus is not one spiritual power among many. Everything holds together in him.
2: Let no one mislead you with empty philosophy or rules about food, festivals and angels. In Christ the whole fullness of God dwells bodily, and you were buried and raised with him in baptism. He nailed the record of our debt to the cross.
We do not need secret extras beyond Christ. Baptism joins us to his death and resurrection.
3: Since you have been raised with Christ, set your minds on things above. Put to death impurity, greed, anger and lying. Put on compassion, kindness, humility and patience, and above all love. Paul gives guidance for wives, husbands, children and servants.
"Whatever you do, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus." Holiness is lived at home and at work.
4: Persevere in prayer with thanksgiving. Behave wisely toward outsiders, and let your speech be gracious. Paul sends greetings from his companions, including Luke the physician and Mark.
Ordinary conversations are a chance to witness. The letter is to be read aloud and shared with other churches.
